newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Singapore VLCCs dip, Carib market firms.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Singapore VLCCs dip, Carib market firms.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) freight rates from the Middle East Gulf to Singapore edged down on Tuesday as newer ships got snapped up for Japan and South Korea voyages, brokers said.

"Some ships missed the 'gold rush' last week when rates to the east firmed and are now willing to take a couple of points less in order to get fixed to Singapore where the age of the ship isn't such an issue," one broker said.
He put the rate to Singapore at W70/72.5 against W77.5 earlier in the week, with voyages to Japan at about W80 and to Europe at W62.5.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs continued at around W67.5, while 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) were active, although they have not risen much from the recent W82.5.

Cross-Med Suezmaxes were quiet, with rates dipping to W70/75, and although little was seen done in the cross-Med Aframax (80,000 tonne) sector, brokers said the rate was about W115, confirming signs of strength seen on Monday.
In the western hemisphere, rates firmed on increased inquiry, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W130 against W122.5 on Tuesday, and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W180/185 from W170.
Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes, meanwhile, remained in a trough at W100.
